arguments.heading: What happened at the argument
paragraphs: Texas argues the Fair Housing Act requires proof of intent.
Inclusive Communities argues the law bans policies with unequal effects.
Justice Kagan questioned the statutory language regarding adverse effects.
Justice Ginsburg asked about the congressional goal of ending discrimination.

paragraphs: The dispute centers on the Fair Housing Act. Texas claims the statute requires proof of intent. Inclusive Communities claims the statute covers disparate impact.

sections.heading: What each side wants
paragraphs: Texas wants the Court to limit the law to intentional discrimination.
Inclusive Communities wants the Court to uphold liability for unequal effects.

paragraphs: This case defines the scope of federal fair housing protections. It determines whether policies with unequal racial outcomes violate the law. The outcome shapes housing policy nationwide.
